reason: The only Jan, C01 (Jan sv Joh), is a deceased estate in the 1830s, but this man died in 1867. The other owners are a woman or men with clearly different given names.
Neither owner, Hendrik Ferdinand nor Petrus Rasmus, matches the given names Lourens Marthinus.
C02 is an exact match on Lodewyk Petrus Spies in the same declared district, Swellendam.
No Botha owner bears the names Ernst Adriaan Lodewyk. Theodorus Ernst (Albany) differs in first name and district.

C14 is the only owner named Petrus Gerhardus, in his declared district Graaff-Reinet. The note 'sv Petrus Gerhardus' fits the family naming pattern, and C04 (Willem Sterrenberg sv Petrus Gerhardus) is plausibly his son.
No Erasmus owner is named Antonie or Philippus, or anything resembling those names.
C02 Casper Labuschagne is in Somerset and matches the first name, with the middle name Jeremias omitted. No other Casper is listed.

C05 is the only owner named plain Louis, matching the genealogy exactly; Koonap in Albany lies close to Somerset. The several Somerset owners recorded as 'sv Louis' look like his sons, and C03 Louis Jacobus carries an extra middle name and a son-of-Louis note.
C14 Philip Rudolph Botha in Somerset matches his names and declared district exactly. C12 Rudolph Philip is a deceased estate, whereas this man died in 1875.
The only Nicolaas, C02, is Nicolaas Martinus in Uitenhage. His second name differs from Jacobus and his district differs from Somerset, so the match is too weak.
